history.period: Built 1699 CE per the main consensus; one travel source (Colours of Gujarat) dates it to the 15th century -- conflict flagged
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE -- keep-or-drop decision needed: the Chintamani is a JAIN temple in the Shahpore (Shahpor) locality of Surat, about 3 km from Surat railway station (Shahpore Main Road, Machhali Pith). Dedicated to Lord Parshvanath, it is one of Surat's oldest Jain temples, built in 1699 CE during Aurangzeb's reign (the main consensus; a 15th-century date in one source is flagged as conflicting). Local tradition links its founding to honouring the 12th-century Solanki king Kumarpal and his adviser, the Jain preacher-poet-philosopher Acharya Hemachandraji. The exterior is deceptively simple; inside it is famed for exquisite wooden architecture -- carved pillars, brackets and ceilings painted with vegetable-dye murals depicting Acharya Hemachandra, King Kumarpal and other Solanki kings -- a rare treasury of 17th-century Gujarati craftsmanship. No photography inside without the trustees' permission. Jain sect (Shvetambara/Digambara) not verified in consulted sources.

town_description: Surat, on the banks of the Tapi in south Gujarat, is a historic port city and one of India's great diamond-polishing and textile hubs. A trading centre since the Mughal era, it is among the country's fastest-growing cities.

travel.railway: Surat railway station, about 3 km (per Trawell).
travel.road: Shahpore Main Road, Machhali Pith, in the heart of the old city near Variyali Bazar and the Dutch and English cemeteries.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; avoid office hours and Jain festival peaks (parking is scarce, per reviews).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-6:00 PM per Trawell/Gujarat Expert. Free entry; photography inside only with trustee permission.
